correctness.rationale: For p>=2 the scalar Clarkson-type inequality yields the necessary condition r^p+s^p<=1; for p>2 equality is pointwise strict unless the two functions are disjoint. In the strict interior, every infinite-dimensional L_p contains a disjoint normalized sequence; restrictions of finitely many test vectors to its disjoint supports tend to zero, furnishing a common witness. On the boundary, if a weak unit u exists, applying equality to u forces any witness y to be disjoint from u and hence zero, impossible. Conversely, if there is no weak unit, h=sum|x| over the finite test family is not a weak unit, so there is a nonzero positive v lattice-disjoint from h; normalizing v gives exact equality for all tests. For p=2 the parallelogram identity yields the disk. The proof correctly separates strict interior from equality and does not infer an infinite-dimensional statement from the sequence-space example.
